newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-STEINBRENNER SAYS TORRE WILL BE BACK NEXT YEAR.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-STEINBRENNER SAYS TORRE WILL BE BACK NEXT YEAR.

text.p: New York Yankees owner George Steinbrenner, who usually makes news by firing managers, made some news Wednesday by saying he is not firing Joe Torre.
Torre will be back to manage the Yankees next year no matter how the club fares down the stretch, Steinbrenner said.

The owner said he and Torre talked during a three-hour rain delay on Tuesday night that eventually washed out the opener of a crucial series with the Baltimore Orioles. He informed Torre of his decision and made it public with a one-page statement Wednesday.

"I spent a good part of our time together discussing what an outstanding job Joe has done this year," Steinbrenner said. "I especially wanted him to know that, no matter what happens in the season's final weeks, the second year of his contract will be honoured and he will return to manage the Yankees in 1997. He deserves it."
"I guess I was surprised by our conversation, but the fact (that he asked me back) doesn't surprise me," Torre said. "I'm looking forward to coming back."

After Buck Showalter was forced out last year, Torre signed a two-year deal, becoming the club's 14th manager in 23 years under Steinbrenner. Torre has guided the Yankees to the brink of their first American League Eastern Division title in 15 years.
Despite numerous injuries and an unsettled pitching staff, Torre has directed the Yankees to a 85-64 mark, three games ahead of Baltimore as the teams opened a three-game series.

"I was happy that, if there was a question, it was addressed," Torre said. "I said last week that it was not my concern. My concern is what is on the field between now and the end of the year. Hopefully, that's November."
The Yankees have been without pitchers David Cone and Melido Perez, starting second baseman Pat Kelly, starting shortstop Tony Fernandez and left fielder Tim Raines for all or most of the season.

"Look at the number of players we've had on the disabled list, especially our projected top starting pitchers," Steinbrenner said. "Those losses have been devastating, but he kept this club together. He's a native New Yorker and he's shown that mental toughness that New Yorkers appreciate."
Torre has done more than keep the club together. With a boost from former New York Mets stars Darryl Strawberry and Dwight Gooden, the Yankees led the Orioles by 12 games on July 28.

But Baltimore caught fire while New York slumped, leading to a rash of trades by general manager Bob Watson that brought Cecil Fielder, Charlie Hayes and Graeme Lloyd to the Yankees. The Orioles cut the deficit to 2 1/2 games before the Yankees beat Toronto on Monday.

"I know as well as anyone that no team among the contenders is 12 games better than the other teams in its division, especially in what I consider the toughest division in all of baseball," Steinbrenner said.
"I'm very happy with the job Joe's done and I thought it was important that he know that so the matter can be put to rest," Steinbrenner said.
However, the owner offered Watson no such confidence vote.
"I was never very good in track and field," Steinbrenner said. "But I learned that you clear one hurdle at a time."
